intro: Receive Stripe test webhooks on a local FlyEnv site. No public domain or tunnel is required.
installFirst: Install a Stripe CLI version from Version Manager, then connect your account.
loginHelp: Connect in your browser and select your Stripe account or sandbox. Stripe CLI manages your credentials; FlyEnv does not ask for your password. Stop the listener before changing accounts.
savedConnectionHelp: Use saved connection checks the selected profile's existing CLI login without opening a browser. Authorize / update access starts browser sign-in and uses the user signed into that browser. A saved connection check does not verify webhook-listener permissions.
freshSessionHelp: CLI logout and fresh sessions do not sign your browser out of Stripe. A fresh session replaces the selected connection's CLI credentials. To use a different Stripe user, choose the separate Different Stripe user button and approve in a private window. Add a saved connection first to keep this one. Stop listening before changing connections or logging out.
differentUser: Sign in as a different Stripe user
privateApprovalHelp: Your browser may still be signed into Stripe. Copy the approval link below, open a private/incognito window (or a different browser profile), paste it there, and sign in as the intended Stripe user. Compare and approve the pairing code in that window. FlyEnv is waiting for approval; it has not opened your default browser. This replaces only the selected connection's CLI session.
approvalCopied: Approval link copied. Paste it into your chosen browser window.
connectionsHelp: Saved connections use separate Stripe CLI profiles. Select one, then Use saved connection to reuse its login. Authorize / update access is for signing in or changing access. FlyEnv stores labels and preferences; Stripe CLI manages credentials. Previously opened terminals retain their selected connection.
duplicateConnection: A connection with that name already exists.
connectionAdded: Connection saved. Choose Authorize / update access for the first sign-in.
connectionBusy: Stop the Stripe listener and finish the current account, terminal or data action before changing connections or telemetry.
disconnectConfirm: Clear this connection's CLI credentials and revoke its CLI session where supported? Your browser remains signed into Stripe. Other CLI terminals using this connection may be signed out. Saved labels are kept.
disconnected: Selected CLI connection logged out. Your browser remains signed into Stripe. Review any CLI warnings below.
telemetryHelp: Off by default in this plugin. When enabled, Stripe CLI can send command usage, errors, timings, OS/CLI versions and detected AI-agent names. Stripe says it excludes credentials, personal data, paths, source code, argument values and account data. Applies to new plugin commands, listeners and terminals; reopen existing terminals after changing it. This setting affects Stripe CLI only.
listenerAuthFailure: Stripe rejected the listener's credentials or account permissions. A stored session is not proof of current access. Start a fresh CLI session, approve the intended account or sandbox, then start listening again. If the error persists, check your Stripe account permissions.
connectionChecked: Selected saved CLI account checked; browser sign-in was not opened
accountCheckPending: Finish checking the Stripe account before starting another action.
reauthorizationHelp: Stripe CLI found a stored session; this does not guarantee listener access. Finish any account-permission approval in your browser, then click Check connection. If the listener reports an authentication error or 403, use Start a fresh CLI session instead.
pairingCodeHelp: Compare this code with Stripe's browser page. Confirm there only if they match. Waiting for approval for up to 10 minutes.
pairingEnded: This connection attempt has ended. Connect again for a new code; do not approve the old browser page.
urlHelp: Select a site suggestion or enter its complete webhook URL. Replace /stripe/webhook with your application's actual route, and keep its local web server running.
eventsHelp: Leave empty to receive all snapshot events. Uses Stripe test mode / sandbox; live events are not enabled.
skipVerify: Allow an untrusted local HTTPS certificate
secretHelp: Use this CLI signing secret in your local application's webhook configuration. Dashboard webhook endpoints have separate secrets.
noEvents: Start the listener, then make a Stripe test payment to see webhook delivery results here.
timeout: Stripe operation timed out. Check the service status before retrying.
loginPending: Finish connecting your Stripe account before starting the listener.
loginPrecondition: Select an installed Stripe CLI version and stop the listener before connecting an account.
installFailed: Stripe CLI installation failed. Check your connection and try again.
testDataHelp: Create Stripe test products, prices, customers and subscriptions using the same account as the listener. These are test objects, not live billing. Keep the listener running to observe the resulting webhooks.
subscriptionHelp: Subscriptions use default_incomplete payment behavior. Stripe may return incomplete until a payment method is added and the first invoice is paid. This form uses test mode; no live charge is created.
creationRetryHelp: A failed response can leave the result unknown. Check Stripe before changing fields or restarting. Retrying unchanged input in this session reuses the same idempotency key.
moreResources: Showing the first 25 objects. Use Stripe CLI for further pages.
finishDataAction: Finish the current test-data action before changing accounts.
selectCLI: Select an installed Stripe CLI version first.
sampleHelp: Choose a fixture to create test objects and events in Stripe. Some fixtures also generate related events. Start the listener and check its delivery log to confirm local receipt.
sampleSent: Stripe created the sample event. Check the delivery log for receipt.
